asked: # hub-look-all-assets — one look from axHub, every app ships every shareable asset Replaces build `hub-only-look` (stopped ~1 min in; merge `claude/hub-only-look` first only if it has commits, otherwise ignore it). Brett, Nov 1 2026 (verbatim): - "The apps should only get appearance from axhub period." - "if you select design package in one app it changes it for all! Any theme change applies to all." - "They all gotta ship all assets that can be shared bruh!" The look is the shared document `shared/settings/appearance.json` on axHub's data server (framework `HubAppearanceSource`; runtime `attachAppearanceSource` / `applyAppearance` / `pushAppearance`). Today an id the hub names that an app doesn't ship is skipped ("not in this app, kept the default"), so apps drift. Measured on main (1156332c): framework/assets has 470 assets, 506 across all apps; console-web ships 415, axhub-web 384, amberx-droid 396, walkthrough-studio 393, demo 446, patches-web 102. PR #224 already made a hub-applied look bring the console back to Main and closed the Active assets pane by default. ## Part A — every app ships every shareable asset 1. Define "shareable": every asset type except the ones that are inherently one app's (decide from schemas/asset-types.json: e.g. `uac-policy`, `settings`, app-specific `help` packs, anything that only makes sense with one app's views). Write the rule into schemas/asset-types.json as a per-type flag (e.g. `"shared": false`) so it is data, not code, and mirror it in the Kotlin kernel. 2. One source of truth for shareable assets: framework/assets (+ framework/brand-library). Assets that live only in one app today but are shareable (e.g. axhub-web's `context-menu/axhub-web`, `nav-menu/axhub-web`, `toolbar/axhub-web`; console's `branding/amberx-brand-014`, `interface/amberx-signature`; whatever the diff finds) move into framework/assets. Where an app copy differs from the framework copy with the same id, keep the newer/app-tuned one in the framework and report each conflict. 3. Apps get the full shared set automatically at build time (vite plugin / the bake step / `framework/cli/app-assets.mjs` — pick the cleanest; prefer generated over hand-copied files so they can never drift again). App-local copies of shared assets are removed from apps/*/src/assets. Apps keep only their own non-shared assets. 4. CI check (framework/cli check script wired into existing checks): fails if any app is missing a shareable asset, or if an app holds its own copy of one. 5. Android (`framework/android`, `apps/amberx-droid` native parts): same set, same rule. 6. Patches: if its edited baked files block this, move the edits into the framework where they're plain improvements; otherwise report exactly what blocks it. ## Part B — appearance only from axHub 1. Remove the follow switch: `APPEARANCE_FOLLOW_KEY` (`axf.hub.appearance.follow`), `appearanceFollowing` / `setAppearanceFollowing` / `syncAppearanceFollow`, the `appearance.hub` action, the "Get the look from axHub" row (framework/libs/settings, framework/libs/hubstatus), help packs. Clear any saved `false` on start (one-time, logged). 2. Console interface tabs (`apps/console-web/src/interfaceTabs.tsx`, `InterfaceScope`): tabs drawing the app under an interface's own look break the rule. Main only; no tab bar with one tab; default `console.interfaceTabs` = []. Applying an interface still works via `applyInterface` (goes to the hub). Remove `scoped()` and its tests if nothing else needs it. 3. Remove `AXF_APPEARANCE_HUB=off` / `appearanceHub: 'off'` (console server + `apps/console-web/src/hubAppearance.tsx`). No hub = waiting screen (decided Oct 20 2026). 4. Every AmberX app attaches the hub source unconditionally (no `if (manifest.developer?.hub)` gate; default `DEFAULT_HUB`). hubsync's `off` look state goes (`own` stays: still the hub). 5. Look tweaks kept on one device today (Sliders, per-asset tokens, `isAppearanceSetting` keys, `scope: 'device'` look keys) must reach the hub and apply…
